title: Cardinal I — The Primacy Of The Idea
says: The starting point and the measure of any mechanism is the best form known to the field; what already exists adapts to it, and the cost of change is never an argument.

title: Cardinal II — Every Mechanism Is Growth-Oriented & Open
says: Every mechanism grows by declaration and is never narrowed, hardcoded or closed; a closed enumeration or a privileged rung is a defect.

title: Cardinal III — One Truth Has One Home
says: Every truth is declared in exactly one place and everything else is a projection of it; a copy is removed, never synchronised.

title: Cardinal IV — A Declaration Never Executes; An Interpreter Never Decides
says: A declaration states what is true and carries no behaviour; an interpreter states how anything is done and holds no policy.

title: Cardinal V — The Surface Never Lies
says: What is shown is what is true or an honestly declared absence, never a fabricated zero, a silent blank or a success that was not observed.

title: Cardinal VI — The Law Set Grows By Declaration
says: The law set grows by declaration in two directions: a concept seen twice is promoted to its home, and a question the doctrine cannot answer is declared as a gap where it is met.

title: Cardinal VII — A Name Is Not A Referent; The Boundary Is Measured, Never Assumed
says: A name is not a referent; a boundary is measured once before it is trusted, never assumed.

title: Cardinal VIII — A Seam Carries One Responsibility And Promises Only What It Keeps
says: A seam carries one responsibility and promises only what it keeps; it grows by extension, and every implementation behind it is substitutable without the caller asking which one it got.
